newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan suspends HIV gene therapy research approval.
newsitem.headline: Japan suspends HIV gene therapy research approval.

text.p: Japan's Health Ministry said on Monday it had suspended its approval for research on gene therapy to be conducted on patients with HIV, the virus that causes AIDS.
The research was to have been conducted at Kumamoto University in southern Japan and sponsored by Osaka-based drug maker Green Cross Corp.
A ministry spokesman said the approval was suspended because Green Cross "withheld information that could have negative implications for the ministry's examination of the therapy".

In the therapy, already undergoing clinical tests on a much larger scale in the United States, patients are injected with genes encoding certain HIV proteins to stimulate their immune systems to attack the virus.
The therapy uses HIV-IT(V), a drug under development by a division of U.S.-based Chiron Corp.

A Green Cross spokesman said the research at Kumamoto University had been expected to start in July, and said the company did not know when the research would be able to start now that the ministry had suspended its approval.
